spec.description: Download counts for your Docker Hub and GHCR images over the dashboard time range, grouped per package, with package and collector views. The counts are requests, not people or finished downloads, and on GHCR an automated manifest read counts too.

spec.title: Package downloads
spec.description: Downloads per package over the dashboard time range, with a bar that compares the packages. Docker Hub and GHCR are added together unless Split by registry is on, which gives each registry its own row, named after the package and the registry. A package tracked for only part of the range counts from its first read, so a range that covers the whole history gives each package's total.

spec.expr: label_replace(label_join(label_replace(label_replace(round(sum by (owner, repo${split}) (delta((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"}))[$__range:1m]))), "registry_name", "Docker Hub", "registry", "dockerhub"), "registry_name", "GHCR", "registry", "ghcr"), "package", " · ", "repo", "registry_name"), "package", "$1", "package", "(.*) · ")

spec.title: Downloads per package
spec.description: New downloads for each package, stacked, split per registry when Split by registry is on, and the tooltip names the packages of a bar. A bar spans an hour on a range of a day or less, 6 hours on a week and a day from 30 days. Tall bars after a release are normal, and automated reads move these counts too, because a GHCR manifest read counts as a download. A bar below zero means a registry restated its total lower.

spec.expr: (sum by (owner, repo${split}) (delta((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"}))[$__interval:1m]))) and on () (vector(time()) > $__from / 1000)

spec.title: Downloads in this range
spec.description: Downloads across the selected packages and registries over the dashboard time range. These are request counts as each registry reports them, so automated reads count too, and a registry that restates its total lower reduces the number. A package tracked for only part of the range counts from its first read, and No downloads yet means no two reads of it fall in the range.

spec.title: Change from the range before
spec.description: Downloads in this range against the range of the same length just before it, in percent and as the difference in downloads. The percent is green from 0 up, yellow from -20 to 0 and red below -20, and the difference beside it keeps the text colour. A rise with no release behind it usually means an automated reader started polling. No earlier range yet means the counts do not reach back to the start of the range before.

round(sum(delta((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"}))[$__range:1m])) - sum(delta((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"}))[$__range:1m] offset $__range))) and (count(max_over_time((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"} offset $__range))[1d:1h] offset $__range)) > 0)

spec.title: Data age
spec.description: Time since the selected registries were last read successfully, for the registry and collector read longest ago. registry-stats reads every hour by default and the colours assume it: green is under 120 minutes, yellow from 120 minutes and red from 360 minutes, which means reads are failing or a collector stopped. Not reported yet means no successful read has been published.

spec.title: Recent pushes
spec.description: The 10 GHCR packages pushed most recently, newest first, from the "Last published" time each package page shows. Every push moves it, signatures, attestations and branch tags included, so a push is not always a release. Docker Hub publishes no push time, so only GHCR packages are listed. No pushes yet means no package page stated a time.

spec.title: Registries out of step
spec.description: Packages one registry has and the other definitively lacks at the last complete read, each status naming its collector, plus an Unknown row when a read was stale or incomplete or a collector stopped reporting. Packages pair by owner and name, and a GHCR name with a slash in it is never compared, because Docker Hub cannot hold one. With owner/* on both registries, a package you publish to one on purpose stays listed while your configuration covers it. A read counts as stale after 2 hours, which assumes the default hourly check, and No package missing means every read was fresh and complete, which a collector that reads one registry also shows.

spec.title: Images nobody pulled in this range
spec.description: Packages whose count did not change at all over the dashboard time range, with their total, one row per package, or per package and registry with Split by registry on. A package here has no readers, not even automated ones, so pick a long range such as 30 days before you retire one. A count a registry restated lower is a change and keeps its package off the list, and a package appears only once every registry it is on reported it before the range began.

spec.expr: label_replace(label_join(label_replace(label_replace(sum by (owner, repo${split}) (max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"})) and on (owner, repo${split}) (sum by (owner, repo${split}) (changes((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"}))[$__range:1m])) == 0) unless on (owner, repo${split}) (max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"}) unless on (owner, repo, registry) max by (owner, repo, registry) (max_over_time(registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"}[1d] offset $__range))), "registry_name", "Docker Hub", "registry", "dockerhub"), "registry_name", "GHCR", "registry", "ghcr"), "package", " · ", "repo", "registry_name"), "package", "$1", "package", "(.*) · ")

defaults.noValue: Every package was downloaded in this range

spec.title: Downloads by registry
spec.description: New downloads on each registry, stacked, in bars of an hour on a range of a day or less, 6 hours on a week and a day from 30 days. Downloads in this range gives the exact total, for one registry when the Registry filter picks it. A jump on one registry alone points at an automated reader or a release that reached one registry first. A bar below zero means a registry restated its total lower.

spec.expr: (label_replace(label_replace(sum by (registry) (delta((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"}))[$__interval:1m])), "name", "Docker Hub", "registry", "dockerhub"), "name", "GHCR", "registry", "ghcr")) and on () (vector(time()) > $__from / 1000)

spec.title: Movers against the range before
spec.description: The 5 packages whose downloads grew most and the 5 that fell most, comparing the dashboard time range with the range of the same length before it. A rise reads green and a fall red. GHCR counts every manifest read, so automated polling moves these numbers as much as people do, and a mover rarely needs an action. A package is listed only once it was reported before the range before began.

spec.expr: label_replace(label_join(label_replace(label_replace(topk(5, round(sum by (owner, repo${split}) (delta((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"}))[$__range:1m])) - sum by (owner, repo${split}) (delta((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"}))[$__range:1m] offset $__range))) > 0 and on (owner, repo${split}) sum by (owner, repo${split}) (max_over_time((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"} offset $__range))[1d:1h] offset $__range))) or bottomk(5, round(sum by (owner, repo${split}) (delta((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"}))[$__range:1m])) - sum by (owner, repo${split}) (delta((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"}))[$__range:1m] offset $__range))) < 0 and on (owner, repo${split}) sum by (owner, repo${split}) (max_over_time((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"} offset $__range))[1d:1h] offset $__range))), "registry_name", "Docker Hub", "registry", "dockerhub"), "registry_name", "GHCR", "registry", "ghcr"), "package", " · ", "repo", "registry_name"), "package", "$1", "package", "(.*) · ")

spec.title: Registry data age
spec.description: Time since each registry was last read successfully, for the selected collector read longest ago. Green is under 120 minutes, yellow from 120 minutes and red from 360 minutes, which assumes the default hourly check, and red means reads of that registry are failing. Not reported yet means no successful read has been published.

spec.title: Last read complete
spec.description: Whether every listing and package read of the last check came back with an answer, per registry, for the selected collector that did worst. Green Yes means nothing was left unknown. Yellow No means a listing was cut short or failed, or some package could not be read, so Registries out of step shows Unknown and the container log names the cause. Not reported yet means no check has finished.

spec.title: Images left out
spec.description: Images beyond the first 250 owner/repo names, which registry-stats does not detail: they get downloads but no push time or presence series. Names are taken in alphabetical order, so the last ones miss out, and listing fewer images brings them back. The value is the selected collector with the most, and green is none and yellow is 1 or more. Not reported yet means no check has finished.

spec.expr: max(sum by (job, instance) (max by (job, instance, source) (registrystats_image_details_omitted{job=~"$job"})))

spec.title: Checks passed and failed
spec.description: Checks per registry across the selected collectors: passed in blue for Docker Hub and purple for GHCR, failed stacked on top in red and orange. A bar spans an hour on a range of a day or less, 6 hours on a week and a day from 30 days, and the legend total adds up the bars. Each collector checks once an hour at the default interval, so no bar means no check finished, and a check at either edge of the range can fall outside the bars. A failed check lost a whole listing or most of its package reads, so any red or orange bar is worth a look at the container log.

spec.expr: (label_replace(label_replace(round(sum by (source) (max by (job, instance, source) (increase(registrystats_collects_total{job=~"$job"}[$__interval])))) - round(sum by (source) (max by (job, instance, source) (increase(registrystats_collect_errors_total{job=~"$job"}[$__interval])))), "name", "Docker Hub", "source", "dockerhub"), "name", "GHCR", "source", "ghcr")) and on () (vector(time()) > $__from / 1000)

(label_replace(label_replace(round(sum by (source) (max by (job, instance, source) (increase(registrystats_collect_errors_total{job=~"$job"}[$__interval])))) > 0, "name", "Docker Hub", "source", "dockerhub"), "name", "GHCR", "source", "ghcr")) and on () (vector(time()) > $__from / 1000)

spec.title: Check duration
spec.description: How long a full check of both registries takes, in minutes, as the median and the 95th percentile over the day before each point. GHCR pages are spaced 2 to 5 seconds apart and Docker Hub requests half a second apart, so the time grows with the number of images. A climb with no new images means slower or retried requests.

spec.title: Counts that went down in this range
spec.description: Packages whose count is now below its highest value in the dashboard time range, with how far it fell, per registry. A registry restating its total, or a page read that returned a wrong number, causes this, and the download figures of the range are lower by that much. The shipped alert RegistryStatsPullCountRegressed fires on a fall within 2 days. No count went down means every count kept its high.

defaults.noValue: No count went down in this range

spec.title: Exporter up
spec.description: Whether your Prometheus server could scrape registry-stats at its last scrape. Green Up is healthy, red Down means the target is unreachable. Not scraped means no scrape target matches the selected job.

spec.title: Restarts in this range
spec.description: How many times a registry-stats process started again within the dashboard range, added up across the selected collectors. Green is none and yellow is 1 or more, and a count that grows without deploys means the container keeps restarting. Not scraped means no process metrics arrived.

spec.title: Memory
spec.description: Resident memory of the registry-stats process, with the trend over the range. It grows with the number of images tracked and stays flat between checks, so a steady climb across days points at a leak. Not scraped means no process metrics arrived.
